claims.text: R0976 is a full professor at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technology, Department of Food Preservation Engineering, with fields in food engineering, packaging and predictive microbiology, and profile keywords covering shelf life, modified atmosphere packaging, berries, cold chain and predictive models.
limitations: Profile self-description only; fields and keywords are declared, not independently verified.
Affiliation and department are profile metadata and were not cross-checked against an external register.

claims.text: R0976 co-authored a 14-day, 2 °C study on Serbian-grown raspberries for export markets in which a 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to an ambient-air control, kept firmness above commercial thresholds for 12 days versus 6 days in ambient, and reported marketable sensory scores at day 10; the work informs film permeability selection and predictive shelf-life modelling.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence; full methods, replication and statistics not reviewed.
Raspberry substrate and 2 °C storage (not 2–4 °C transit) and abstracted summary metrics only; the study does not itself demonstrate 14-day, below-1% mould incidence at destination.
Some listed participants on the underlying record have no internal researcher ID, so the complete author list is not established beyond the identity field used.

claims.text: R0976 co-authored a film-screening study of 12 polymeric films differing in OTR and CO₂TR in which headspace equilibrium gas composition was measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days at 2 °C and finite-element gas-permeation modelling was used to confirm headspace trends and predict equilibrium under alternative fill weights; the best film yielded a 55% reduction in mould incidence versus a standard polyethylene control.
limitations: Evidence concerns mixed-berry trays, not the 125 g rPET punnet plus anti-fog lidding film configuration specified in the challenge; transfer requires re-verification.
Abstract-level metrics; the reported film specification values are study results and not validated for this company's format.

claims.text: R0976 co-authored work showing that pre-cooling protocol before MAP sealing changes headspace equilibration speed and Botrytis incidence: forced-air cooling reached target core temperature in 38 minutes versus 210 minutes for room cooling and gave lower Botrytis incidence at day 8, while hydrocooling introduced free moisture that promoted decay.
limitations: Study measured headspace and decay over a 10-day trial; longer-term behaviour is not reported.
Pre-cooling practice at the company's packing houses is unknown to the reviewer.

claims.text: R0976 co-authored a digital-twin study that integrated validated Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic count growth models with temperature and relative humidity sensor streams for Serbian berry cold-chain operations; in a 12-month pilot across 240 consignments, alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments later confirmed with elevated spoilage at destination, with 9% false positives attributed mainly to sensor placement near evaporator coils.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence; sensor hardware, data pipeline and model calibration details are not reviewed.
Results apply to the studied exporter set and climate; performance on the company's own shipment data is not established.

claims.text: R0976 co-authored a stochastic shelf-life modelling study using Monte Carlo propagation of temperature-profile uncertainty from 180 sensor-monitored consignments, whose prediction intervals covered 91% of observed microbiological end-point data, and a feasibility study on sensor-based remaining-shelf-life labelling for Serbian raspberry and blueberry consignments using Arrhenius temperature dependence.
limitations: The stochastic modelling study is on strawberries, not raspberries.
Remaining-shelf-life labelling agreement (±1.2 days for 79% of consignments) is a labelling metric, not a reduction in mould incidence, and is drawn from abstract-level text.

claims.text: R0976's listed openness is industrial PhD supervision and joint projects, and the recorded industry experience is work with three fruit exporters on packaging trials.
limitations: Engagement types are declared preferences, not commitments; no specific availability, budget or contract terms are recorded.
The three past exporter collaborations are unnamed and undated; no overlap with this company is established.

claims.text: Taken together, the evidence covers the challenge's two suspected levers — condensing conditions and OTR/CO₂TR matched to berry respiration — plus the modelling step from measured permeability and headspace data to a film specification, and the translation of shipment temperature/humidity logs into shelf-life estimates. This is a plausible fit for the modelling and trial-design portion of the problem, not proof that the 14-day, below-1%-mould target is achievable in the company's punnet.
limitations: No evidence shows any work on a 125 g rPET shell with heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film specifically.
Micro-condensation inside the punnet is not directly addressed by any registered evidence; it remains an open hypothesis to test.
Semantic support of the retrieved evidence was not assessed by the retrieval system.

claims.text: Bounded pilot: use the last two seasons of shipment temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports to establish the current mould-versus-time baseline and to parameterise existing Botrytis growth models; then run small controlled simulated-transit trials in the company's lab comparing the two existing film grades with one or two OTR/CO₂TR levels selected by gas-mass-balance modelling, measuring headspace O₂/CO₂, condensation and visible mould incidence at intervals up to day 14.
limitations: Trial design, film set and duration are proposals to be confirmed with the company and are not source facts.
Budget is limited; the number of film variants must be reduced to whatever the company can fund in materials and lab time.

claims.text: Proposed milestones: (1) baseline analysis of existing shipment and inspection data with a documented current mould-incidence curve; (2) model-based shortlist of film permeability specifications; (3) simulated-transit trials with headspace and mould-count endpoints; (4) decision on a next-season film specification and any pre-cooling or pallet-level gas-management adjustment. Go/no-go: proceed to a larger format trial only if the shortlisted specification shows a clear and repeatable reduction in day-9-to-day-14 mould incidence versus the current film, alongside headspace gas within target ranges and no increase in condensation or off-condition defect.
limitations: Timelines, numerical thresholds and milestone count are proposals, not commitments or verified achievements.
A controlled simulated-transit result is not a guarantee of destination performance, and the day-14 below-1% target is a company goal, not an evidenced outcome.

claims.text: Validation requires a common baseline: the company's existing film and current seal settings run in the same simulated-transit protocol, with mould incidence scored blind and headspace composition measured by the company's OTR/CO₂TR and headspace instruments, supported by the company's historical destination inspection data.
limitations: Instrument accuracy, sampling plan and statistical power are not established and must be agreed before trials.
Proposed go/no-go criteria are assumptions to confirm, not source-supported targets.

claims.text: Remaining requirements not covered by this evidence: direct work on micro-condensation in heat-sealed rPET punnets, a demonstrated below-1% day-14 mould incidence in the company's own format, and any compostability constraint on the lidding film. These need company-specific trials and, for film material design, additional input beyond the registered evidence.
limitations: The active-packaging evidence involving antimicrobial sachets is on blueberries and is not proposed here as a solution for the company's format.
No registered evidence addresses compostable or recyclable lidding-film reformulation.

summary.text: R0976 (rank 1 in the pool) is a food-engineering and packaging researcher whose registered, attributed work covers modified-atmosphere packaging of Serbian export raspberries, film OTR/CO₂TR screening with gas-permeation modelling, pre-cooling effects on headspace equilibration and Botrytis, and predictive/digital-twin shelf-life modelling from cold-chain sensor data. That aligns with the challenge's stated gap — translating OTR/headspace measurements and shipment logs into a film specification — and with the suspected respiration/micro-condensation mechanism.
The evidence is abstract-level and mostly on other berry formats and substrates; it supports a bounded, company-lab-based pilot, not a guaranteed 14-day, below-1% mould outcome.

technicalRationale.text: Raspberry-specific MAP work under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reached the 14-day window with a 63% Botrytis reduction versus air and 12 days of firmness above commercial thresholds — a relevant experimental template for the company's 2–4 °C punnet scenario.

Film screening combined with finite-element permeation modelling and headspace equilibrium measurement provides the exact method chain the company lacks: measured OTR/CO₂TR plus headspace data converted into a specification, with fill-weight sensitivity.

Digital-twin and stochastic shelf-life modelling convert the company's temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports into Botrytis-risk and remaining-shelf-life estimates, with reported flagging performance in Serbian berry chains.
Pre-cooling findings indicate a second, non-film lever (equilibration speed, moisture management) that may matter as much as film permeability.

cooperationScope.text: Proposed contribution: data analysis of the last two seasons' shipment logs and inspection reports; model-based ranking of film permeability specifications compatible with the 125 g rPET punnet and heat-sealed anti-fog lidding film; design and statistical analysis of small simulated-transit trials; and documentation of a candidate film specification.
Milestones: baseline mould-incidence curve; permeability shortlist; simulated-transit trial results; written specification recommendation and go/no-go decision before the next season.

validation.text: Baseline: current film grade and seal settings under identical simulated-transit conditions. Measurements: headspace O₂/CO₂ at defined intervals, condensation assessment, visible mould incidence scored blind at days 9, 12 and 14, plus gas-permeability verification on the company instruments.

Proposed go/no-go: proceed to a larger trial only if the shortlisted specification produces a clear, repeatable reduction in day-9-to-day-14 mould incidence versus baseline with headspace within target ranges and no worsening of condensation. These thresholds are proposals to be agreed with the company.

constraints.text: Engagement is limited to what R0976 declares: industrial PhD supervision and joint projects. Any consultancy, budget, IP or publication terms must be negotiated; none are recorded.

Required company inputs: two seasons of temperature/humidity logs and destination inspection reports, punnet and film samples, seal settings, and access to the OTR/CO₂TR and headspace instruments. Trial funding is limited, so the number of film variants and trial arms must be kept small.

The work is constrained to the raspberry/berry MAP context in the evidence; transfer to the company's specific punnet format and to a compostable lidding film is not evidenced and would require separate evaluation.

unknowns.text: Open questions: which two film grades were trialled and what OTR/CO₂TR they had; the actual measured temperature profile in transit and at destination; the definition and counting method for 'visible mould'; whether pre-cooling at the Serbian packing houses is forced-air, hydrocooled or ambient; whether any compostability requirement is binding for this lidding film; and how much lab time and materials budget is actually available.
